/ai-form-builder/job-application-form.note: why_description: Untrue generalization about competitors (catalogue rows 7 and 8): 'Form tools stop at the submit button.' Jotform, which is in this page's own table and top 10, sells Jotform Tables, Approvals and workflow routing after submit. -> Drop the claim about other tools and state what Emergent builds, e.g. 'Emergent builds the form, the applicant table and the manager alerts as one app, and the code is yours.' (stay within 25 words). | hero_description / features_subheading / why_description: The same sentence appears three times in three sections: 'Emergent builds the job application form and its applicant database' (hero), 'Emergent builds the form and the record it feeds' (features_subheading), 'Emergent builds the form and the applicant pipeline behind it as one app' (why). The sibling creator-application uses the same shape twice ('Emergent builds the form, scoring, review queue, and the database behind it', 'Emergent builds the form, the screening, and the creator roster as one build you own'), so this reads like a template with the nouns swapped (HUB_RULES 2b rhythm, rubric voice/distinct). 'the record it feeds' is also vague. -> Keep the hero sentence. Replace the second sentence of features_subheading with something only this section says, e.g. 'Below are the six sections Emergent drafts and what each application turns into once it is submitted.' Rewrite why_description without 'Emergent builds the form and...' (see the why_description fix above). | feature_1: 'Each field gets a proper input.' is vague filler that does not say what the reader gets (HUB_RULES 2a: 'Name the trigger, the field, the tool'). -> Name the inputs, e.g. 'Start dates get a date picker, phone numbers a phone field, and work history repeats for every past job.' Re-balance the body to 165-182 characters. | tab_content_1 / tab_image_1 / prompt_chip_2: The copy says 'Applicants then tap the shifts they can work on a weekly grid and give a start date', and the chip says 'Availability Grid'. The image has no grid: it shows three weekend chips (Sat AM, Sat PM, Sun PM), with the start date above them. The rubric's images test needs the copy and image to match word for word. -> Either redraw the main panel as a small weekly grid (days by AM/PM, with Sat AM, Sat PM and Sun PM selected) placed below the start date, or change the copy to 'Applicants give a start date, then tap the shifts they can work.' and rename chip 2 to match (e.g. 'Shift Availability'). | tab_content_2 / tab_image_2: The copy says 'Each nurse or medical assistant gives a license number and the state that issued it', but the image's Grace Liu row reads 'CMA' with no state. That is also the truth: CMA is a national certification (AAMA), not a license a state issues, so the copy is wrong about medical assistants. -> Change the copy to 'Each nurse gives a license number and the state that issued it; medical assistants give their certification.' Alternatively, replace the CMA row with a state-licensed role (e.g. 'LPN, Kentucky') and limit the sentence to nurses. | tab_content_3 / tab_image_3: The copy says 'Anyone short of the posting's minimum tenure is told before they submit', but the image's timeline puts 'Tenure checked' after 'Application received 9:12 AM', which shows the check happening after submission. -> Reorder the steps to 'Tenure checked (18 months in role, minimum 12)' then 'Application submitted 9:12 AM' then 'Current manager alerted' then 'Hiring manager review'. Or relabel step 1 'Tenure confirmed before submit'. | tab_image_3 (mini card): The mini card reads 'Separate from outside hires', while the copy says 'a table kept apart from outside candidates'. 'Hires' means people already hired, not external applicants, so the label is wrong. -> Change the mini card sub to 'Separate from outside candidates'. | tab_image_4: The story is that the list is 'Sorted by must-haves' (work authorization and salary range), and the hero says 'Each one meets every must-have'. Yet the shortlisted rows show unrelated or partial facts: Mara Cole 'Remote, portfolio attached' (a portfolio is not a must-have), Tom Baker 'Office, salary in range' (no authorization), Lena Fox 'Remote, work authorization' (no salary). The panel does not show why these three passed. -> Make every shortlisted sub show both must-haves, e.g. 'Remote, authorized, salary in range'. Keep Ivan Petrov 'No work authorization' as the one on hold. | feature_5 / why_table: One thing has three names on the page: 'applications' (body), 'a table that never caps submissions' (feature_5) and 'Response limits' / 'Where responses live' (table rows). HUB_RULES 2a says to use the same term for the same thing. -> feature_5: 'in a table that never caps applications'. Regenerate the table with row labels 'limits=Application limits' and 'data=Where applications live' (the same label override as 'uploads=Resume uploads'). | faq item 4 (Can I download a job application form PDF?): The top 10 are blank PDFs and DOCs (rocklinusd, circuit7, Iowa, DS-1950), so this question asks for a blank form. The answer says 'Yes.' and then describes only filled copies of submitted applications, which misleads the searcher. The blank PDF only shows up four items later, in FAQ 8. -> Answer the blank form first: 'Yes. The form Emergent builds can give you a blank PDF of the same questions to print, and it can save each submitted application as a filled PDF ending with the applicant's typed signature and date.' Keep the Haddad_RN.pdf naming line. Trim FAQ 8 to the free-to-start and paper-intake points so the two don't repeat. | faq item 12 (Do I need separate job application forms for each role?): The question is about roles, but the evidence is about locations: 'Separate copies per location tend to drift: one store rewrites its availability question and the others never hear about it.' The answer then concludes about roles ('one form that branches by position'). The middle sentence argues a different question. -> Make the example about roles, e.g. 'Separate copies per role tend to drift: the cashier form gets a new availability question and the stock-clerk form never does.'
